references.text: Also addresses carrion (נְבֵלָה) and how one becomes unclean by eating them, which expands on the prohibition against eating fat from such animals.
Prohibits priests from eating carrion or animals torn to pieces (נְבֵלָה וּטְרֵפָה), the same categories mentioned in Leviticus 7:24.
Prohibits eating meat from animals that have been torn to pieces (טְרֵפָה) and commands that they be thrown to the dogs.
Contains the fundamental prohibition against eating fat (חֵלֶב), which is a permanent statute for all generations.
The preceding verse, which forbids eating fat from cattle, sheep, and goats, providing context for verse 24.
The following verse warns that anyone who eats fat from animals sacrificed to the Lord shall be cut off from their people.
Prohibits eating carrion but allows it to be given or sold to foreigners, confirming that such animals could be used for other purposes.
Ezekiel declares that he has never eaten carrion or torn flesh, showing that this prohibition was an important part of Jewish purity practice.
Reiterates the prohibition for priests against eating carrion or torn birds or animals.
